figures.title: What the selector decides
figures.caption: Figure 1. Decision and observed outcomes. A selector accepts a paid direct draft or requests a fresh thinking solve from the question alone. Escalation pays for both calls. The matrix shows the four scored outcome categories among all 400 direct/thinking pairs on the 50-question repeat panel. A pair matches sample indices; the two modes use different seeds. These are observed counts, not predictions or utility-gain labels. Every pair contributes once, and cell area does not encode its count.

figures.title: Questions and draws have different roles
figures.caption: Figure 2. Sampling and study roles. The primary panel contains 50 questions, eight independent draws per mode, and 800 responses, paired into 400 states by sample index. Each outer fold fits on 40 questions and evaluates on ten excluded questions. The diagram shows the four-draw A-to-B direction; B-to-A reverses the draw halves while retaining question separation. Direct drafts change across draws. Later controls and post-hoc diagnostics reuse these 50 questions. The separate 64-question panel supplies the 11-question cap subset and the development states used to refit the guard before its 228 fresh questions. The latter link indicates design influence, not shared questions or replication. Box sizes are schematic.

figures.title: The tested learners miss their utility targets
figures.caption: Figure 3. Recorded four-draw utility differences on the same 50 questions. Panel A compares the primary learner with a baseline selected within training from accept, escalate, and confidence. Panel B compares later families selected within training with confidence. Dots and bars show the reported means and conditional 90% whole-question bootstrap intervals. Fits and actions stay fixed; intervals omit refitting and research-selection uncertainty and have no joint coverage. Negative values favor each stated comparator. Different comparators prevent a pooled effect. Exact values remain in Tables 2 and 3; all displayed screens failed.

figures.title: Policy accuracy and output cost
figures.caption: Figure 4. The separate two-solver diagnostic, averaged across draw directions. Rows align each policy's scored accuracy and charged output tokens for 128 paired states in the same 64 question groups. Marks show reported point estimates; no accuracy or token interval is inferred. Both calls are charged on escalation. The 4/64 and 24/64 counts identify questions with positive realized gain in at least one of two draws at lambda=.05, not positive expected-gain labels. Tokens are not equal compute units across solver sizes. No population model-size effect or latency advantage is established.
